questions.question: Does $\int_1^{\infty} \frac{1}{x^p} \, dx$ converge for $p = 0.5$?
questions.explanation:
For p-integrals $\int_1^{\infty} \frac{1}{x^p} dx$:
- Converges if $p > 1$
- Diverges if $p \leq 1$

Since $p = 0.5 < 1$, the integral diverges.

Check: $\int_1^{\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} dx = \lim_{t \to \infty} [2\sqrt{x}]_1^t = \lim_{t \to \infty} (2\sqrt{t} - 2) = \infty$

questions.question: Evaluate $\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \, dx$.
questions.explanation:
This is Type 2: discontinuous at $x = 0$.

$$\int_0^1 \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} dx = \lim_{\epsilon \to 0^+} \int_{\epsilon}^1 x^{-1/2} dx$$

$$= \lim_{\epsilon \to 0^+} [2\sqrt{x}]_{\epsilon}^1 = \lim_{\epsilon \to 0^+} (2 - 2\sqrt{\epsilon}) = 2$$

Converges to $2$.

questions.question: Evaluate $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx$.
questions.explanation:
The Gaussian integral is a famous result:
$$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-x^2} dx = \sqrt{\pi}$$

This is proven using polar coordinates in multivariable calculus and is a fundamental result in probability and statistics.
